gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a 'Bluetooth' spec on a premium portable CD player can mean the wrong direction or the wrong SKU: FiiO's own DM13 page says the standard DM13 cannot transmit Bluetooth (only the DM13 BT sends to headphones, in aptX HD, aptX LL, aptX or SBC), and the Shanling EC Play's LDAC works only when it receives from a phone, because it sends to headphones in SBC only.
standout_why: I compared against rottenwifi.com, macmyths.com, trettitre.com and howtovr.com/best-cd-players-with-bluetooth. av.com returned 403 and was not read. None of these four mentions the FiiO DM13 or the Shanling EC Play. None gives a transmit codec for any player: rottenwifi and macmyths say outright that they have no codec data, and howtovr's only codec is SBC for the Panasonic SC-PM270. They do separate transmit from receive, but only for budget players such as the Jensen, Megatek and Sunoony, and they never point out that one model name can come with or without a transmitter. None of them says what output or mode a battery-hour rating was measured on, except for POFOTO on howtovr. ChatGPT's own answer explains TX versus RX in general terms but showed the DM13 card without saying that only the BT version transmits.
decides: This confirms the FiiO DM13 BT as the premium pick for someone sending CDs to Bluetooth headphones or a speaker. It transmits aptX HD and aptX LL, while the EC Play sends SBC only. It also adds a buying rule: the listing must say 'DM13 BT', because the standard DM13 has no transmitter. The EC Play is the better choice only if the shopper wants to stream from a phone into the player (LDAC receive) or needs the longer 12 h rating. For the cheap tier, the battery figures normalised to Wh show the Coby CD201 carries about 39% of the DM13's stored energy (5.55 vs 14.25 Wh), so its 6 h rating is the one to treat with caution.

findings.label: Bluetooth transmit by version
findings.value: Standard version: no Bluetooth transmit. BT version: transmits aptX, aptX Low Latency, aptX HD, SBC
findings.note: FiiO's page says, verbatim: 'Standard version cannot transmit Bluetooth.' It also says some headphones and speakers support SBC only, and some car systems are not supported. It does not list any receive mode or receive codecs.

findings.label: Bluetooth codecs by direction
findings.value: Transmit: SBC only. Receive: LDAC, AAC, SBC. Bluetooth 6.0
findings.note: The LDAC on the spec sheet applies only to phone-to-player streaming. CD audio sent to headphones goes out in SBC.

findings.label: Transmit codec, reviewer confirmation
findings.value: SBC in transmitter mode (no LDAC, no AAC)
findings.source_title: Shanling EC Play Review – Chris Love, Mobileaudiophile (4 July 2026)
findings.note: Chris Love, verbatim: 'in Transmitter Mode it sends Bluetooth out using SBC and not LDAC or even AAC.'

findings.label: Battery, rated, normalised to Wh
findings.value: 10 h rated; 3,750 mAh at 3.8 V = 14.25 Wh
findings.note: FiiO does not say which output (single-ended, balanced or Bluetooth transmit) the 10 h was measured on; its footnote says only 'Data from FIIO labs'. Wh = 3.75 Ah × 3.8 V.

findings.label: ESP anti-skip buffer, maker statement
findings.value: ESP switch present; FiiO publishes no buffer length
findings.note: FiiO says only that enabling ESP 'can improve playback stability'. Our current page's '60 s buffer' cell is not supported by the maker page (see unsourced).

findings.label: Battery, rated vs reviewer estimate
findings.value: 12 h rated (3,450 mAh); reviewer estimate about 7–8 h under heavy use
findings.source_title: Shanling EC Play Review – Chris Love, Mobileaudiophile (4 July 2026)
findings.note: Chris Love: '12 hours is best case scenario, favorable conditions, low gain, tiny screen off' and 'I have no hard-line test… my gut says 8 in total, maybe 7'. This is an estimate, not a measurement. Shanling's page gives neither the cell voltage nor the test output.

findings.label: Price at launch
findings.note: Shanling: 'MSRP 199 USD / 220 Euro… (Check with dealers for USA pricing)'. This is a launch MSRP, not today's store price.

findings.label: Battery, rated, normalised to Wh and max draw
findings.value: Up to 6 h rated; 3.7 V × 1,500 mAh = 5.55 Wh; power consumption 1.52 W max, which works out to about 3.7 h at maximum draw
findings.source_title: Coby CD201 Wireless Anti-Skip CD Player manual, Specifications (ManualsLib)
findings.note: ManualsLib shows labels and values in separate lists, so the pairing is by order. 5.55 Wh ÷ 1.52 W = 3.65 h. The manual gives no output or mode for the 6 h and no anti-skip seconds. Elsewhere it calls the Bluetooth mode 'Bluetooth Audio-Out' (transmit).

findings.label: Rival coverage of battery conditions and codecs
findings.value: None of the rival pages read gives a transmit codec for a portable player; battery hours appear without the output/mode they were measured on
findings.source_title: Best Portable CD Players With Bluetooth in 2026 – rottenwifi.com
findings.note: Also read on 2026-11-17: macmyths.com (same gaps), trettitre.com (no codecs, no hours) and howtovr.com/best-cd-players-with-bluetooth (POFOTO is the only player with hours split by mode: 19 h Bluetooth vs 9 h CD).

unsourced: FiiO DM13 ESP buffer in seconds: FiiO's product page gives none. Head-Fi posts said to quote FiiO staff ('60 s CD / 120 s MP3, compressed') returned a bot check and could not be read. Our page's '60 s buffer' cell needs a source or should be removed.

FiiO DM13 measured battery life (our page says '~8 h measured'): the Audiophile-Heaven and Headfonics reviews both returned 403. I found no battery figure measured in Bluetooth transmit mode for the DM13 BT.
Shanling EC Play anti-skip buffer length: not on Shanling's page or in the Mobileaudiophile review.
Shanling EC Play cell voltage (needed for Wh): not stated by Shanling.
Coby CD201BK anti-skip seconds: not in the manual's spec table. The only figures I found were retailer listings for other Coby models.
GPX BCB119B speaker output in watts: no maker page found. Retailer listings give only 6× C batteries and a 33 ft Bluetooth range, and I did not open them.

Current prices: Amazon search via amzcheck.py returned nothing (walled). I did not check a FiiO or Coby US maker store. Whether ChatGPT's 'DM13 … with Bluetooth (Skylight…)' $184.99 card is the BT or the standard SKU is unconfirmed: the only claim found is a Head-Fi search snippet, which I did not open.
